title: Bawling out Cab during the Bill Robinson show
summary: While conducting the Cotton Club show, Thomas rebukes a nervous Cab for heckling, later apologizes, and explains Cab picked up bawling out from Rudy Vallee.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Fantastic. Now, Foots, tell me what the show was like. Who was in the show?
I can't remember everybody. Was Bill Robinson in that show?
Bill Robinson. Sure. It featured Cab Calloway...
Oh, that's the show I had to bawl Cab out in.

I think it was of Bill's (?)s. Because that's the time when I was the conductor. I didn't have to be in the band, so I was just conducting the band. And Cab got off the wall. He just was nervous about who was going

to be the star in the show, and he had to show his authority that this was his... He knew it was his band, but he just wasn't in it at that time. I had charge of it, and I knew it! And he heckled us a couple of times. I bawled him out in front of the whole show. I just laid him out. And I said, 'Man, leave us alone. We know what we're doing.' He shut up, too. He knew he was wrong, but he was just nervous. But I did have the sense to go back later and apologize. Because I'm bawling my boss out! But he just didn't have nothin' to do with the show. So why try to make something wrong with the band?

He picked that jazz up from Rudy Vallee. I saw when he made the change. We used to do broadcasts or something, and Rudy Vallee one day... There was a place where Rudy Vallee was rehearsing his band. And he was making big money. And oh, he just got an opportunity to bawl the guys out. And he was giving them the devil...

And Cab saw it. So he picked it up. Any time he got a chance to bawl the band out, he'd do it. But this one time he bawled the wrong time, because I had charge of the band, and knew it, and the whole Cotton Club knew that I was the conductor, and they wrote him out of the show. So he had nothin' to do but sit there and wait til his time come to
rehearse(?). And he got off the wall.

I bawled him out... I had to... I knew what was wrong, see. So I went back and I said, "Fess, I'm sorry, but you were just wrong." And (?) that show... He had hives. When the show opened, he had hives. Because he just got nervous, you know. Because he was worrying about whether he was going to get the best report...whether he or Bill Robinson... And it was two different personalities. Bill Robinson had his thing, and he had his thing -- so why worry about Bill Robinson? And he got so nervous, he had hives all over his body.
